title: How to Use the Adecco Salary Guide 2018 PDF for Hourly to Annual Pay Conversion
description: Learn how to convert hourly wages to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and references to the Adecco Salary Guide 2018 PDF.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks; National Minimum Wage from July 2026 is $26.44/hour ($1,004.90/week).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full‑time employee on a 38‑hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements. The National Minimum Wage for casual employees from July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 + 25% loading). When using our timesheet, check the casual loading box to add the 25% on top of your base rate – do not type a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at the rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is calculated on your ordinary time earnings (usually your base hourly rate × hours worked) and is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for super guarantee purposes is $270,830 per year. For example, on the National Minimum Wage annual gross of $52,245.44, super would be an additional $6,269.45.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to convert it to an annual figure so you can compare jobs, budget, and understand your tax obligations. The standard approach in Australia is to assume a 38‑hour week (full‑time) and a 52‑week year. The formula is simple: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**.

For part‑time or casual workers, the same formula applies using your actual weekly hours. If you work irregular hours, you can estimate an average weekly total. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps you run the numbers quickly.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38‑hour week is the standard full‑time week under most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. The 52‑week year reflects the number of weeks in a calendar year, even though many employees receive four weeks of paid annual leave. The conversion assumes you are paid for all 52 weeks, which is typical for salaried employees and for hourly workers who take paid leave.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage (NMW) is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award‑free employees. Most workers are covered by a modern award, which may have higher minimum rates for specific classifications.

For example, the Miscellaneous Award (MA000104) has multiple levels. While the 2018 rates from that award are now outdated, they illustrate how awards structure pay. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides up‑to‑date pay guides on its website. Always check the current award for your industry.

### The Adecco Salary Guide 2018 PDF: A Historical Reference

The **Adecco Salary Guide 2018 PDF** is a recruitment industry publication that listed salary ranges for various roles. It can give you a sense of market rates from that year, but it should not be used for current pay decisions. Official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), and the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) provide more reliable, up‑to‑date information. For instance, the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for full‑time adult ordinary time employees is $2,083.70 per week – far above the 2018 guide figures.

When you see a salary figure in an old guide, remember that wages have increased each year through annual wage reviews. The NMW in 2018 was $719.20 per week ($18.93 per hour) – a 3.5% increase that year. By 2026, it has risen to $1,004.90 per week. Always use current data.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, at the NMW: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This can help you align your budget with your pay cycle. Our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates tax and Medicare deductions for any pay period.

## Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax‑free threshold means many part‑time workers pay little or no tax. Use our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page to see how tax affects different income levels.

## Superannuation on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional cost to the employer. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For a worker earning $52,245.44 (NMW annual), super adds $6,269.45. If you earn above the cap, super is only paid on the first $270,830. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more details.

## Using the Timesheet on This Site

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are a casual employee, tick the casual loading box – do not type a rate that already includes the loading. The tool uses the current NMW, tax rates, and super guarantee to give you a realistic estimate.

### A Note on Accuracy

The conversion assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, up to the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide). HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included. This is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability.

## Further Reading

- [Average pay](/topics/average-pay) – Compare your earnings to ABS averages.
- [Casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) – Understand the 25% loading and when it applies.
- [Job pay](/topics/job-pay) – See how different industries and roles pay.

Whether you are negotiating a salary, planning a budget, or checking your pay rate, the hourly‑to‑annual conversion is a fundamental skill. Use current official data, and treat historical guides like the Adecco Salary Guide 2018 PDF as a starting point only. The Fair Work Ombudsman and the ATO are your best sources for accurate, up‑to‑date information.
